definition.def: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.
examples: I like a big challenge and they don't come much bigger than this.
The new government's first challenge is the economy.

definition.def: If someone rises to the challenge, they act in response to a difficult situation which is new to them and are successful.
examples: Such projects illustrate the company's ability to rise to the challenge of an evolving marketplace. [+ of]
They rose to the challenge of entertaining 80 schoolchildren for an afternoon.

definition.def: A challenge to something is a questioning of its truth or value. A challenge to someone is a questioning of their authority.
examples: The demonstrators have now made a direct challenge to the authority of the government. [+ to]

definition.def: If you challenge ideas or people, you question their truth, value, or authority.
examples: I challenged him on the hypocrisy of his political attitudes. [V n + on/about]
The move was immediately challenged by two of the republics. [be VERB-ed]

definition.def: If you challenge someone, you invite them to fight or compete with you in some way.
examples: A mum challenged her to a fight after their daughters fell out. [VERB noun + to]
He left a note at the scene of the crime, challenging detectives to catch him. [VERB noun to-infinitive]
We challenged a team who called themselves 'College Athletes'. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If someone is challenged by a guard, they are ordered to stop and say who they are or why they are there.
examples: The men apparently opened fire after they were challenged by a patrol. [be VERB-ed]

examples.sentence: Using alternative fuels and improving energy efficiency is thus both an ecological necessity and a technological challenge.
The major challenge of the project lay in the fact that the Forth & Clyde Canal is situated 35 metres below the level of the Union Canal.
Abstract art offers both a challenge and the freedom to play with different interpretations.
And with certain other migrating species, the challenge is complicated further - by vastly greater distances traversed, more jurisdictions, more borders, more dangers along the way.

Participants in the online debate argued that our biggest challenge is to address the underlying causes of the agricultural system's inability to ensure sufficient food for all, and they identified as drivers of this problem our dependency on fossil fuels and unsupportive government policies.

Such findings present a big challenge to British conservation, which has often selected arbitrary assemblages of plants and animals and sought, at great effort and expense, to prevent them from changing.
A new challenge to vehicle production is now on the horizon and, again, it comes from automation.
The weight of the enormous mass was a challenge for the builders, who placed the stones at an inward incline in order to prevent the monument breaking up."
The real mental challenge comes from playing multiple games at once in the head.
